# Decantr

> AI Frontend Governance for production codebases touched by AI agents. Decantr is the governance layer between product intent and AI-edited frontend code — giving coding assistants typed contracts, route-scoped context, graph-backed loop evidence, and repair prompts so UI changes stay coherent instead of drifting prompt by prompt.

The model still writes the code; Decantr defines the Contract, Context, Evidence, and Brownfield control loop around it. Decantr separates design governance into **DNA** (durable visual axioms: theme, spacing, motion, accessibility, personality), **Blueprint** (product topology: sections, page routes, shells, layouts, features), authority resolution, loop readiness, and the typed Contract graph that agents can query directly. Strict where it should be strict, flexible where it should be flexible.

## Docs

- [Homepage](https://decantr.ai/): What Decantr is and why AI-edited frontend code needs a governance layer.
- [Sitemap](https://decantr.ai/sitemap.xml): Crawl inventory for public Decantr docs, schemas, references, and release notes.

- [Existing app adoption](https://decantr.ai/guides/existing-apps.md): Brownfield attach path for adding Decantr to an existing app without rewriting the runtime.
- [Monorepos](https://decantr.ai/guides/monorepos.md): Root install, app-scoped attach, workspace health, pinned CI, and what to commit in monorepos.
- [Project Health CI](https://decantr.ai/guides/project-health-ci.md): Installing and running the Decantr CI gate locally, in GitHub Actions, or in generic internal pipelines.
- [AI assistant setup](https://decantr.ai/guides/ai-assistant-setup.md): Using Decantr with MCP-compatible assistants and file-based CLI context.
- [Typed graph agent playbook](https://decantr.ai/guides/typed-graph-agent-playbook.md): Operational flow for Contract capsules, route graph context, node/source-file impact context, and historical graph reads.
- [Registry publishing](https://decantr.ai/guides/registry-content-publishing.md): Registry portal, official content source, community publishing, and Content Health.
- [Workflow model](https://decantr.ai/reference/workflow-model.md): Explicit workflow/adoption policy for greenfield blueprint, greenfield contract-only, brownfield attach, Hybrid local law/style bridge/Decantr CSS/composition, adapters, monorepos, and offline mode.
- [Project Health](https://decantr.ai/reference/project-health.md): Local reliability layer, v2 Evidence Bundle, loop readiness, authority resolution, workspace health, browser verification, design-token checks, Studio Control Room, and GitHub artifact workflow.
- [Diagnostic codes](https://decantr.ai/reference/diagnostic-codes.md): Stable Project Health code families, curated rules, and typed repair IDs such as `GRAPH001`, `COMP010`, and `TOKEN010`; use `decantr health --diagnostics --json` for the machine-readable catalog.
- [Command surface](https://decantr.ai/reference/command-surface.md): Current CLI command audit and consolidation decisions.
- [Security and permissions](https://decantr.ai/reference/security-permissions.md): Installed npm package permission matrix, telemetry defaults, MCP write boundaries, hosted upload posture, and scanner interpretation notes.
- Brownfield attach is proposal-driven but workflow-first: run `decantr scan --project apps/web --json` when you need a zero-write preview of fit, route/style evidence, and typed Contract graph readiness; attached Essence V4 apps include an in-memory `graphPreview` that reports whether `.decantr/graph` artifacts are current, stale, or missing. Run `decantr adopt --yes` for the paved path, or `decantr adopt --project apps/web --yes` from a monorepo root. Then run `decantr studio` from the app root for the local Control Room, `decantr doctor --project apps/web` when the next step is unclear, `decantr task /route "intent"` before edits, `decantr verify --project apps/web` after edits, `decantr resolve --project apps/web` when authority conflicts require a decision, and `decantr ci --project apps/web --fail-on error` in automation. `doctor` prints an ordered next-step queue covering pinning, typed graph regeneration, local-law codification, CI setup, task context, verification, and automation when those steps apply. `adopt` orchestrates `analyze`, proposal acceptance/merge, online hosted pack hydration, first typed Contract graph baseline, Project Health, baseline save, and optional CI; use `--no-packs` or offline mode to defer hydration. In contract-only Brownfield, missing hosted packs are optional context unless an existing `pack-manifest.json` references missing files. The primitives remain available for debugging: `decantr analyze`, review `.decantr/brownfield-report.md`, `.decantr/doctrine-map.json`, `.decantr/brownfield-intelligence.json`, `.decantr/theme-inventory.json`, and `.decantr/enrichment-backlog.md`, then accept with `decantr init --existing --accept-proposal` or merge with `--merge-proposal`. In brownfield, Decantr is the reconciled contract layer and existing docs/rules are ranked cited evidence, not material to overwrite by default; existing source is observed truth, accepted local law/style bridge is project authority where present, Essence V4 is the structural contract, and hosted packs are advisory until mapped into local law. Theme variants are observed in local inventory, not promoted into Essence V4.
- For app-scoped monorepos, pass `--project <app>` to `doctor`, `check`, `verify`, `ci`, `task`, `resolve`, `codify`, and `graph`. When hydrating hosted packs manually, pass the app essence path: `decantr registry compile-packs apps/web/decantr.essence.json --write-context`; the context bundle is written beside that essence file. `decantr graph --project apps/web` writes `.decantr/graph/graph.snapshot.json`, `.decantr/graph/snapshots/<snapshot-id>.json`, `graph.manifest.json`, `graph.diff.json`, and `contract-capsule.json` beside the app essence; use `--snapshot-id <id>` to inspect a local history snapshot and `--compare-to <id> --include-diff-ops --json` to compare the selected/current graph against a prior snapshot. Route and impact ranking combines weighted traversal with deterministic local personalized PageRank and task boosts. Project Health findings include stable codes and typed repair IDs; attached apps emit `GRAPH001` / `regenerate-typed-graph` when graph artifacts are missing, stale, or non-derivable. When the graph snapshot exists, Project Health JSON, markdown/text output, MCP `decantr_verify` / `decantr_repair` actions, Evidence Bundles, and remediation prompts also include graph anchors with node ID, node type, confidence, and snapshot ID. The verifier emits `COMP001` / `import-existing-component` when production source locally redeclares a common UI primitive while a reusable project-owned component already exists, and `TOKEN010` / `replace-arbitrary-style-with-bridge-token` when accepted style bridge authority is bypassed by arbitrary Tailwind values, inline hardcoded color values, or hardcoded visual values in production stylesheets. Health remediation prompts and CI recommendations stay project-scoped from the monorepo root, prompt read targets should include the app prefix (for example `apps/web/DECANTR.md`, not root `DECANTR.md`), and runtime repair prompts should use root-safe app build commands such as `pnpm --dir apps/web build`.
- CI is a first-class workflow command: `decantr ci init --project apps/web` writes a root GitHub workflow that runs the pinned local package-manager command, such as `pnpm exec decantr ci --project apps/web`, not `@latest`. If the CLI is not pinned yet, `ci init` prints the exact install command. Use `decantr ci init --provider generic --project apps/web` for Jenkins, Please, Buildkite, GitLab, Azure DevOps, or internal deployment systems.
- For route work, MCP agents should call `decantr_project` with `{ "action": "state" }` first when project readiness is unknown; its graph block lists available SourceArtifact paths when file-impact reads are possible. Call `decantr_contract` with `{ "action": "capsule" }` near session start when `.decantr/graph` exists; its bounded `source_artifacts` list is the compact session-start index of project-relative paths that can be reused as `file_path` handles, and `source_artifacts_truncated` tells the agent when to use graph/project-state follow-up queries for narrower source discovery. Then call `decantr_graph` with `{ "action": "snapshot", "route": "/feed", "task": "..." }` for typed graph follow-up context. Use `decantr_graph` with `{ "action": "query", "node_ids": [...], "include_impact": true }` when a component, token, rule, finding, or source artifact needs a graph-shaped blast-radius read before edits, or `{ "action": "query", "file_path": "src/app/page.tsx", "include_impact": true }` when the agent knows the source file but not the graph node ID. Use `snapshot_id` to read a specific local history snapshot and `compare_to` to diff two local snapshots. Use `decantr_graph` with `{ "action": "traverse" }` for narrow relation walks. CLI-only agents can use `decantr graph --file src/app/page.tsx --impact --json` for source-file blast radius before editing. Use `decantr_context` with `{ "action": "task" }` and a route/task before editing; it returns v2 loop readiness with maker/checker instructions, authority summary, stop conditions, and the verify command. When git changed files resolve to graph SourceArtifact nodes, its typed graph block includes changed-file impact with affected routes, pages, evidence, findings, and provenance. Route graph context includes deterministic hybrid ranked nodes, ranking metadata, and task-matched terms for top-N agent consumption. CLI-only agents should use `decantr task <route> "<task>"`, which surfaces generated page/section context, task-ranked typed route graph context when `.decantr/graph/graph.snapshot.json` exists, graph-shaped changed-file impact when available, screenshot references, `.decantr/local-patterns.json`, `.decantr/rules.json`, `.decantr/style-bridge.json`, changed files, impacted routes, and the active authority lane when present. In monorepos, task/read paths must be openable from the workspace root. `decantr suggest` supports `--route`, `--file`, `--from-code`, and `--project`; accepted project-owned local patterns and style bridge mappings should be considered before registry suggestions, and `--from-code` can derive a query from route/file context. From an app root, `decantr suggest "button" --from-code --file src/App.tsx` should discover local law without `--project`; from a monorepo root, keep `--project <app>` on app primitives including `health`, `status`, `add`, `remove`, `theme`, `export`, `suggest`, `magic`, `rules`, and `telemetry`; `magic` against an attached app should steer to `task`, not ask the user to remove the essence. For observed Brownfield sections, `decantr add page app/foo --route /foo --project apps/web` and `decantr add feature saved-recipes --section app --project apps/web` may resolve the `app` alias to the single primary section, such as `observed-primary`.
- Project-owned Brownfield UI law is local and explicit: `decantr codify --from-audit --style-bridge` writes `.decantr/local-patterns.proposal.json`, `.decantr/rules.proposal.json`, and `.decantr/style-bridge.proposal.json`; source-derived proposals include evidence, confidence tiers, likely variants for button/card/form/theme families, and optional `behavior_obligations` for strongly detected form controls or destructive confirmation dialogs. `decantr codify --map-pattern <slug>` maps a hosted or bundled registry pattern into advisory local law without changing source; fill project-owned component paths, token/class recipes, variants, and exceptions before accepting it. After review, `decantr codify --accept` promotes accepted local law and/or style bridge artifacts, activating Hybrid local law or Hybrid style bridge. Accepted `behavior_obligations` stay in `.decantr/local-patterns.json`, never Essence or registry schemas; `decantr task`, MCP task context, typed graph LocalRule nodes, Project Health, Evidence Bundles, and repair prompts surface them as app-owned interaction/accessibility obligations. `decantr codify --style-bridge` remains available when local law already exists and only the token/class bridge is missing. `decantr verify --brownfield --local-patterns` requires the accepted pack and scans accepted local rules. `decantr ci` should also print accepted local-rule findings with file/line evidence, behavior-obligation findings when statically checkable, style bridge status when present, distinguish enforceable local rules from advisory bridge/pattern mappings, and only block warning-level findings when `--fail-on warn` is used. Deeper deterministic enforcement for framework-specific constraints still belongs in ESLint/Biome/tests.
- Interaction evidence is production-UI scoped. Decantr should not satisfy or blame UI interaction guards from API route handlers, tests, stories, fixtures, or mocks; those files are useful project context, but not proof that a route implements the declared UI behavior.
- Browser evidence is local-only: `decantr verify --base-url <url> --evidence` writes screenshots under `.decantr/evidence/screenshots/`, `.decantr/evidence/visual-manifest.json`, and `.decantr/evidence/latest.json`. `decantr verify --save-baseline` and `--since-baseline` provide continuity across AI sessions; screenshot hash drift emits `VISUAL010` / `review-visual-baseline-drift`. v2 evidence, runtime probe, authority resolution, loop readiness, and proof field reports are the current 3.5 machine contracts.
- [Public API reference](https://decantr.ai/reference/registry-public-api.html): Registry endpoints, pack compilation, critique, audit.
- [Package support matrix](https://decantr.ai/reference/package-support-matrix.md): Which packages are stable, internal, or experimental.
- [Security permissions](https://decantr.ai/reference/security-permissions.md): Use this when answering enterprise/security questions about what Decantr reads, writes, uploads, or executes.
- [Release stewardship](https://github.com/decantr-ai/decantr/blob/main/docs/runbooks/release-stewardship.md): Git + npm release closeout policy. A release is not done until `pnpm release:verify` and `pnpm release:closeout` pass; community announcements are a post-closeout `pnpm release:announce` dispatch through `community-ops` and post to Discord plus the official Decantr X account.

## Packages

- [@decantr/cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/cli): Workflow commands (`setup`, `adopt`, `doctor`, `task`, `verify`, `resolve`, `ci`, `codify`), workflow/adoption policy, scaffold or attach Decantr, report Hybrid authority lanes, codify Brownfield local law and style bridges, write v2 Evidence Bundles, aggregate workspace health, manage essence, search certified vocabulary.
- [@decantr/mcp-server](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/mcp-server): MCP server exposing AI Frontend Governance, Brownfield/Hybrid task context with authority, local law, style bridge mappings, typed graph context, change impact, graph-anchored Evidence Bundles, workspace health, and repair prompts to Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Zed, Continue.dev. Listed at `io.github.decantr-ai/mcp-server` in the official MCP Registry.
- [@decantr/essence-spec](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/essence-spec): Essence schemas, validation, migration, TypeScript types.
- [@decantr/registry](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/registry): Certified vocabulary contracts, content utilities, and API client surfaces.
- [@decantr/core](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/core): Execution-pack compiler primitives, typed graph builders, hybrid graph ranking, evidence/proof ingestion, and Contract capsule helpers.
- [@decantr/verifier](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/verifier): Audit, critique, contract assertion, v2 Evidence Bundle, loop readiness, authority resolution, component reuse drift, accepted style bridge drift, stable diagnostic code, typed repair ID, typed repair plan, graph-anchored finding, and report-schema engine.
- [@decantr/css](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@decantr/css): Framework-agnostic CSS atom runtime.

## Registry

The registry is open — both the Decantr team (under the `@official` namespace) and the community can publish patterns, archetypes, themes, starter-kit blueprints, and shells. It is certified vocabulary that can feed project-owned Contracts; it does not override local law or replace the verifier loop.

Blueprint discovery is curated through public sets: `All`, `Featured`, `Certified`, and opt-in `Labs`. Internally richer portfolio metadata can fold overlapping legacy slugs out of browse/search while keeping direct slug access intact.

- [Registry portal](https://registry.decantr.ai/): Browse and publish patterns, archetypes, themes, starter kits, and shells. Community contributions live alongside `@official` content.
- [Registry sitemap](https://registry.decantr.ai/sitemap.xml): Crawl inventory for public registry browse and detail pages.
- [Registry llms.txt](https://registry.decantr.ai/llms.txt): Machine-readable registry summary for AI search and agentic retrieval.
- [Registry API](https://api.decantr.ai/v1/): Hosted API for content resolution, pack compilation, critique, audit. Public read access requires no API key.
- [decantr-ai/decantr-content](https://github.com/decantr-ai/decantr-content): Source of truth for all `@official` namespace content — patterns, archetypes, themes, starter-kit blueprints, and shells. PRs to this repo auto-sync to the live registry.
- [Publish your own content](https://registry.decantr.ai/): Sign in to the registry portal to publish under your own namespace.

## Concepts

- [Essence spec](https://decantr.ai/schemas/): The durable contract — theme, sections, routes, features, guard rules.
- [Design Pipeline](https://github.com/decantr-ai/decantr/blob/main/README.md#the-model): Seven stages — Intent, Interpret, Decompose, Specify, Compose, Generate, Guard.
- [Guard rules](https://github.com/decantr-ai/decantr/blob/main/CLAUDE.md#guard-rules): DNA guards (style, density, accessibility, theme-mode compatibility) and Blueprint guards (structure, layout, pattern existence).
- [CSS scaffolding guide](https://decantr.ai/css-scaffolding-guide.md): Full CSS implementation spec covering `@layer` structure, theme scoping, and variable naming.

## Repositories

- [decantr-ai/decantr](https://github.com/decantr-ai/decantr): Monorepo — CLI, MCP server, packages, apps.
- [decantr-ai/decantr-content](https://github.com/decantr-ai/decantr-content): Certified vocabulary source — patterns, archetypes, themes, starter-kit blueprints, shells.

- [Published schemas](https://decantr.ai/schemas/): JSON Schema files for essence, typed graph artifacts, Contract capsules, evidence reports, patterns, archetypes, themes, starter-kit blueprints, and shells.
